title: "Evolutionary Contradictions: A search for truth beyond the directly observable." 
---

What is observable, is not often the complete picture. We often observe a cellular enviornment, and witness immense complexity, perhaps even disorder and nonsense. When viewed at this scale, the aperture distorts vision: our ability to understand visual information and infer further processes. From outward however, it is clear; cells are the tiny soldiers of all things. But even this may not be entirely true; Quantum Physics and Advanced Mathematics reveal a deeper story.

So if our observation is not the final arbiter; what we observe (e.g., semantics) is not guaranteed to be true at whole scale (e.g, pragmatics)

What are some of the most problematic contradictions of Darwin's Theory on Evolution, that cannot Logically be explained from a perspective of pure Evolutionary reasoning?

For example, Siphonophores and certain classes of cells, exhibit "immortal" abilities. The problem of death, implies time is not objective; it is experiential. Cyclical. Einstein basically worked through Equations to discover that Spacetime was curved (which is another fascinating problem; how are we able to manipulate abstract representations of the world, that reveal a truth, not otherwise observable? Does it imply our natural abilities are extended by our tool-making abilities? Fascinating problem.)

Another classic case is Consciousness; it appears to be neither mere Genetic Mutation, nor Evolutionary necessity; Consciousness (by Neuroscience and Psychology) appears to present more Entropy and Volatility, than non-conscious or non-fully-aware forms of life. They seem to balance eco-systems and food chains plenty well... it is almost as if Consciousness is a disturbance of the natural way of life; Instinct vs. Intuition vs. Intellect .

A being whom is conscious, will inevitably become conscious (aware) of threat, danger and inescapable limitations of their condition; this is what Philosphers essentially titled "The Human Condition."

However, before Philosophy, and even before Human Consciousness, let's explore contradictions in the Animal, Cellular (or even Celestial and Mathematical) Domains, which afford a necessary repositioning of a purely Materialistic worldview; several artifacts about life do not follow the Logical reasoning laid out by a purely evolutionary, deterministic-based world.
